t:
(a)

        (1) 
The item relating to section 509 in the table of contents of the Regional Rail Reorganization Act of 1973 (45 U.S.C. 701 et seq.) is amended to read as follows:


“Sec. 509. Payment, audit, and report.”.


 
 
        (2) 
The table of contents of the Regional Rail Reorganization Act of 1973 (45 U.S.C. 701 et seq.) is amended by inserting immediately after the item relating to section 509 the following new item:


“Sec. 510. Railroad hiring.”.



  
    (b) 
Section 102(16) of the Regional Rail Reorganization Act of 1973 (45 U.S.C. 702(16)) is amended to read as follows:


“(16) 
‘Secretary’ means the Secretary of Transportation or the designated representative of the Secretary;”.



 
    (c) 
Section 201 of the Regional Rail Reorganization Act of 1973 (45 U.S.C. 711) is amended—

        (1) 
by amending subsection (d)(2) to read as follows:


“(2) 
three Government members, who shall be (A) the Secretary, acting directly or at any time through the Deputy Secretary of Transportation, the General Counsel of the Department of Transportation, the Federal Railroad Administrator, or the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Railroad Administration, (B) the Secretary of the Treasury, acting directly or at any time through an officer of the Department of the Treasury who has been appointed with the advise and consent of the Senate, and (C) the Chairman of the Commission, acting directly or at any time through the Vice Chairman of the Commission; and”;



 
        (2) 
striking out “through their respective Deputy Secretaries” from the first sentence of subsection (i) and inserting in lieu thereof “in the case of the Secretary, through the Deputy Secretary of Transportation, the General Counsel of the Department of Transportation, the Federal Railroad Administrator, or the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Railroad Administration, and, in the case of the Secretary of the Treasury, through an officer of the Department of the Treasury who has been appointed with the advise and consent of the Senate”; and
 
        (3) 
by striking out the first sentence of subsection (j)(4).
  
    (d) 
Section 501 of the Regional Rail Reorganization Act of 1973 (45 U.S.C. 771) is amended—

        (1) 
in paragraph (6), by inserting immediately after “disability,” the following: “failure to work due to strike, fire, flood, snowstorm, hurricane, earthquake, tornado, or other similar natural occurrence that causes a suspension of operations in whole or in part and precludes performance of the work which would be performed by the incumbents of the positions to be abolished or the work which would be performed by the employees involved in the force reductions,”; and
 
        (2) 
by striking out “and” at the end of paragraph (10), by striking out the period at the end of paragraph (11) and inserting in lieu thereof ”; and”, and by adding at the end thereof the following new paragraph:


“(12) 
‘compensation’ means earnings in employment subject to the Railroad Retirement Act.”.



  
    (e) 
Section 507 of the Regional Rail Reorganization Act of 1973 (45 U.S.C. 777) is amended by inserting “, section 509(b), or section 509(c)” immediately after “section 504(d)”.
 
    (f) 
The first sentence of section 403(d)(1) of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 563(d)(1) is amended by striking out “if such State” and all that follows through “service”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that amending the membership of a board signals an advisory body with outside participants. But the only membership language here concerns the three Government members (Transportation, Treasury, and the Commission Chairman) and which federal officers may act for them, all of whom are inside the federal government. The rest of the section is table-of-contents, definitional, and technical amendments, with no comment period, hearing, outside consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: three Government members, who shall be (A) the Secretary, acting directly or at any time through the Deputy Secretary of Transportation, the General Counsel of the Department of Transportation, the Federal Railroad Administrator, or the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Railroad Administration

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Regional Rail Reorganization Act to define 'Government members' of a Commission as specific federal officials (Secretary of Transportation, Secretary of Treasury, etc.). It does not require consultation with or participation by non-federal entities. The other amendments relate to table of contents, definitions of 'Secretary', and definitions of 'compensation' and disability, none of which involve outside participation.
qwen_block.s: three Government members, who shall be (A) the Secretary, acting directly or at any time through the Deputy Secretary of Transportation, the General Counsel of the Department of Transportation, the Federal Railroad Administrator, or the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Railroad Administration, (B) the Secretary of the Treasury, acting directly or at any time through an officer of the Department of the Treasury who has been appointed with the advise and consent of the Senate, and (C) the Chairman of the Commission, acting directly or at any time through the Vice Chairman of the Commission
qwen_block.b:
Temptation: The text mentions a "Commission" and its "Chairman" and "Vice Chairman" in subsection (c)(1). One might assume this Commission includes outside members or that the Commission's existence implies participation. However, the text only defines who the *Government members* are (federal officials). It does not describe the composition of the entire Commission, nor does it mandate consultation with outsiders. The rest of the text deals with table of contents amendments, definitions of "Secretary," and definitions of "compensation" and disability. These are internal administrative or definitional changes.

Resolution: The section primarily amends definitions and internal government structures (specifying which federal officials serve as government members of a commission). It does not require consultation with, or participation by, non-federal entities (states, tribes, public, companies) in a decision-making process. The mention of the Commission is limited to identifying its government members, which are inside the federal government. Therefore, there is no participation as defined.

opus.w: This section makes technical amendments: it changes the table of contents and definitions, and it names which federal officials serve as the board's Government members. Those members are all federal officials, so the change stays inside the government. The deletion of the 'if such State' language in subsection (f) does not create any consultation with states, and the section has no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, outside advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: three Government members, who shall be (A) the Secretary, acting directly or at any time through the Deputy Secretary of Transportation
opus.b:
I'm labelling this section **No**: nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.

1. **The tempting reading:** Subsection (c) changes who sits on a board, and subsection (f) amends a provision that mentions a "State". Both could look like outside-party participation.
2. **Why it fails:** The board change covers only the "three Government members". Each is a federal official, such as the Secretary of Transportation, the Secretary of the Treasury, or their deputies. Subsection (f) only deletes words ("if such State" and what follows). It creates no consultation or process involving states.
3. **The rest of the section:** It updates the table of contents, the definitions and cross-references. Nothing creates a comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body with outside members, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section primarily contains technical amendments to the table of contents, definitions, and internal agency procedures. The only reference to a body's composition (Section 201) explicitly lists 'Government members' who are federal officials (Secretary of Transportation, Secretary of Treasury, etc.). There is no requirement for consultation with, or inclusion of, non-federal parties in the decision-making process described in this text.

However, the text explicitly lists the "Government members" as high-ranking federal officials (Secretary of Transportation, Secretary of Treasury, Chairman of the Commission).
